> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #349 adds implicit follow-up intent routing for agent-labeled issues and PRs.
- It closes #348, a scoped child of #124, by allowing unmentioned comments/reviews on `agent`-labeled targets to wake the router.
- The intended behavior is answer-only: an intent gate returns `respond` or `ignore`; `respond` maps to the inline `answer` route and `ignore` posts nothing.
- The PR also updates docs, tests, prompt wiring, comment metadata forwarding, and communication-rubric selection for this path.

## Review
The implementation matches the intended product shape, but the current workflow runs the implicit intent agent before answer-route authorization, which expands denied unmentioned commenters into a privileged model execution path. That needs a branch fix before shipping.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Intent gate runs before answer authorization | BLOCKING | `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` runs `followup-intent` with the repo token and `permission_mode: approve-all` before `resolve-dispatch` checks whether the commenter may use `answer`. Denied callers should be skipped before any model/tool-capable agent task starts. |
| Follow-up runtime/provider setup is ordered too late | WARNING | Runtime setup installs CLIs from the initial dispatch-provider resolution, but the follow-up gate later resolves the `answer` route provider. A route override can select a provider whose CLI was not installed. |
| Edited implicit comments can duplicate answers | WARNING | `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review_comment` edits are eligible for implicit follow-up handling without previous-body comparison or per-comment dedupe. A typo edit to a question that already got an implicit answer can trigger another answer. |

## Progress
- The PR already forces implicit `respond` decisions to `answer` and ignores model-proposed alternate routes.
- Tests cover labeled/unlabeled/disabled implicit candidates, `respond`, `ignore`, and post-classifier unauthorized answer drops.
- Docs now describe `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_INTENT_MODE`, `agent` label activation, and the answer-only limitation.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted inline comments for the blocking pre-authorization gate and the edited-comment duplicate-answer risk; no threads were resolved or minimized.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Intent gate runs before answer authorization</summary>

**Cause:** `extract-context` only requires a known association before marking `implicit_followup=true`, then `agent-router.yml` runs `followup-intent` at `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L295-L311`. The answer-route policy is applied later in `resolve-dispatch.ts#L165-L190`, after the model has already run.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a deterministic preflight that applies the `answer` route policy before `followup_provider` and `followup_intent`; skip silently when denied. Also reduce the classifier’s permission surface if it only needs to classify text.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed on severity: one treated this as consistent with existing triage ordering, while another flagged the new unmentioned denied-caller path plus `approve-all` as blocking. The current diff supports treating it as blocking because authorization occurs after a privileged agent task starts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Follow-up runtime/provider setup is ordered too late</summary>

**Cause:** `setup-agent-runtime` runs from `steps.provider.outputs.install_*`, where `provider` is resolved for `dispatch`. The follow-up path later resolves `route: answer`, so `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY.route_overrides.answer.provider` can choose a different provider after setup has already decided which CLI to install.

**Candidate solutions:** Resolve the follow-up/answer provider before runtime setup when the implicit path is possible, or make runtime setup install the union of required providers for the active path.

**Comments:** This is already captured in the rubrics review as the main partial-score gap.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Edited implicit comments can duplicate answers</summary>

**Cause:** `isSupportedImplicitFollowupEvent` accepts `edited` for unmentioned issue and PR review comments, but the implicit path does not have the explicit mention false-to-true guard or another dedupe mechanism.

**Candidate solutions:** Limit the first slice to created comments and submitted reviews, or add a previous-body/state guard before supporting edited implicit follow-ups.

**Comments:** One reviewer noted this is not a regression from explicit answer edits, but the implicit path is noisier because users did not mention the agent.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The blocking authorization ordering issue and the two workflow hardening gaps are concrete branch changes suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Add deterministic answer-route authorization before `followup_provider` / `followup_intent` can run for implicit follow-ups.
- [ ] Ensure runtime setup installs the provider selected for the implicit answer-route intent gate.
- [ ] Add an edit dedupe/previous-body guard, or restrict implicit follow-ups to created/submitted events.

@sepo-agent /answer 

frankly the logic here is a bit fussy. can you walk me through what's going on inside the agent-router?

Yep. The key idea is: **the router now separates “may this event wake Sepo?” from “should Sepo actually answer?”**

For PR #349’s implicit follow-up path, the flow is:

1. **`agent-entrypoint.yml` is the broad wake-up filter.**  
   It still wakes on `@sepo-agent`, but now also wakes for unmentioned comments/reviews when:
   - `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_INTENT_MODE` is not `disabled` / `false`
   - sender is not a bot
   - event is a new issue comment, new PR review comment, or submitted PR review
   - target already has the fixed `agent` label  
   See [`agent-entrypoint.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml#L48-L87).

2. **`agent-router.yml` prepares both possible runtimes up front.**  
   It resolves the normal `dispatch` provider, and conditionally resolves the `answer` provider for possible implicit follow-ups. Runtime setup installs the union of needed CLIs so an answer-route provider override does not fail later.  
   See [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L160-L210).

3. **`extract-context` decides whether this is a real request candidate.**  
   Explicit mentions stay unchanged. If there is no live mention, it calls the follow-up helper and only sets `implicit_followup=true` for supported labeled events. It also intentionally leaves `requested_route` empty, so an unmentioned comment cannot smuggle in `/implement` or `/review`.  
   See [`extract-context.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.agent/src/cli/extract-context.ts#L191-L267) and [`followup-intent.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.agent/src/followup-intent.ts#L17-L80).

4. **Before any implicit intent model runs, the router preauthorizes `answer`.**  
   This is the safety gate added after review: if the commenter is not allowed to use the `answer` route under `AGENT_ACCESS_POLICY`, the router stops silently before running the follow-up classifier.  
   See [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L249-L262).

5. **Normal dispatch triage is skipped for implicit follow-ups.**  
   Explicit/free-form mentioned requests still go through dispatch triage. Implicit follow-ups instead go through a dedicated `followup-intent` prompt that can only return `respond` or `ignore`, with communication rubrics enabled.  
   See [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L264-L386) and [`followup-intent.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/prompts/followup-intent.md#L17-L37).

6. **`resolve-dispatch` enforces the answer-only contract.**  
   If intent says `ignore`, it emits no route. If intent says `respond`, it forces `route=answer` and re-applies dispatch policy. Any malformed intent output also becomes no route, not a fallback answer.  
   See [`resolve-dispatch.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.agent/src/cli/resolve-dispatch.ts#L86-L201).

7. **Only after that does the normal `answer` job run and post.**  
   The answer route receives the original comment ID/URL plus rubrics, then posts through the existing response path.  
   See [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/bad7e61f045518a03886c0558cd13b218950cf67/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L537-L592).

So the fussy part is mostly defensive layering:

```text
entrypoint wake-up
-> context says explicit mention OR eligible implicit follow-up
-> implicit path preauthorizes answer
-> intent model says respond/ignore only
-> resolver forces respond to answer only
-> answer job posts
```

That avoids the dangerous version of this feature, where an unmentioned comment on an `agent`-labeled thread could accidentally trigger implementation/review/orchestration or run a privileged classifier before route authorization.

- It adds `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_INTENT_MODE` so unmentioned comments/reviews on fixed `agent`-labeled issues or PRs can wake Sepo.

@sepo-agent why removing the comment ids?

They were removed from the PR branch because they had become **duplicate plumbing**, not because we no longer want comment IDs.

What happened:

- This PR originally added `request_comment_id` / `request_comment_url` so the answer agent could know the exact triggering comment/review.
- While the PR was open, `main` gained the same trigger-metadata contract already:
  - [`request_comment_id`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3c78df0c0387504010b91446f9fa6330542c7127/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L64-L70)
  - env export to `REQUEST_COMMENT_ID` / `REQUEST_COMMENT_URL` / `REQUEST_SOURCE_KIND` ([action.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3c78df0c0387504010b91446f9fa6330542c7127/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L362-L364))
  - answer-route wiring in `agent-router.yml` ([router](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3c78df0c0387504010b91446f9fa6330542c7127/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L424-L427))
- Keeping the PR’s copy on top of `main` produced duplicate YAML keys in the merge result, which broke CI.

So the fix removed the **PR-added duplicate copies**. The current PR head keeps the new follow-up/rubric-specific additions, but no longer redefines comment IDs in the answer route block ([current PR head](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c012afa5c7c37a295b0f537b98440df0da97f7e5/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L561-L566)).

Net effect: comment IDs are **not removed from the final merged behavior**. They come from `main`’s existing request metadata contract instead of being added a second time by this PR.
